concepts.name: Direct vs. Indirect Taxes: Incidence and Shifting
key_dimensions: Theoretical distinction between impact and incidence of tax
Why indirect taxes are considered regressive while direct taxes are progressive
UPSC trap: Cases where direct tax burden can be shifted (e.g., corporate tax passed to consumers)
India's revenue composition: Historical shift from direct to indirect dominance and post-GST trends

concepts.name: Progressive, Regressive, and Proportional Tax Structures
key_dimensions: Definitions and examples within Indian tax system (income tax slabs vs. GST on essentials)
Equity principle: Horizontal vs. vertical equity in taxation
UPSC trap: GST being regressive despite being a consumption tax — implications for inequality
Canon of taxation (Adam Smith) and how Indian taxes conform or deviate

concepts.name: Income Tax: Structure, Slabs, and New vs. Old Regime
key_dimensions: Old regime (deductions-heavy) vs. New regime (lower rates, fewer exemptions) — policy rationale
Surcharge and cess (Health & Education Cess) as additions to base tax — constitutional status of cess
UPSC trap: Cess proceeds do NOT go to Consolidated Fund of India in the same divisible pool as taxes
Recent changes: Rebate under Section 87A, revised slabs in Union Budget 2023 and 2024

concepts.name: Corporate Tax: Structure, Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT), and Reforms
key_dimensions: Difference between nominal corporate tax rate and effective rate due to exemptions
MAT (Section 115JB): Purpose — preventing 'zero-tax companies'; how it works
UPSC trap: MAT applies to book profits, not taxable profits — distinction is examinable
2019 corporate tax cut (from 30% to 22%) — rationale, impact on investment and fiscal deficit

concepts.name: Capital Gains Tax: Short-Term vs. Long-Term, Indexation
key_dimensions: Distinction between STCG (Section 111A) and LTCG (Section 112/112A) with holding period thresholds
Indexation benefit: Cost Inflation Index (CII) and its removal/modification in Budget 2024 for real estate
UPSC trap: LTCG on equity above ₹1 lakh taxed at 10% without indexation — post-2018 change
Policy debate: Whether lower capital gains tax promotes investment or creates equity concerns

concepts.name: Goods and Services Tax (GST): Structure and Federal Architecture
key_dimensions: Dual GST model: CGST, SGST, IGST — which goes to whom and under which constitutional provision (Article 246A)
Constitutional amendment: 101st Amendment Act 2016 — what was subsumed and what was kept out (petroleum, alcohol)
UPSC trap: Parliament AND state legislatures have CONCURRENT power to legislate on GST — unique feature
GST Council composition, voting weights, and whether its decisions are binding (Supreme Court ruling in 2022)

concepts.name: GST Rate Structure and Exemptions: Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Four-tier rate structure (5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) plus zero-rated and exempt categories
Inverted duty structure problem: Input taxed at higher rate than output — refund mechanism and sectors affected
UPSC trap: Zero-rated (exporters get refund) ≠ Exempt (no refund of input tax credit) — critical distinction
Compensation cess on luxury/sin goods: Constitutional basis, revenue sharing, and post-2022 continuation debate

concepts.name: Input Tax Credit (ITC) Mechanism under GST
key_dimensions: How ITC eliminates cascading effect (tax on tax) — comparison with pre-GST CENVAT credit
Conditions for availing ITC: Invoice matching, payment within 180 days, eligible goods/services
UPSC trap: ITC NOT available on motor vehicles, food, club membership, works contract for immovable property
Fake invoice and ITC fraud: Policy response — Rule 86B, blocking of ITC, and recent enforcement measures

concepts.name: Customs Duty: Structure, Effective Rate of Protection, and Trade Policy
key_dimensions: Basic Customs Duty (BCD), Social Welfare Surcharge, IGST on imports — layered structure
Effective Rate of Protection (ERP): How tariff on final goods minus tariff on inputs determines actual protection
UPSC trap: ERP can exceed nominal tariff rate — implication for 'Make in India' and infant industry protection
Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) and how customs duty escalation supports domestic value addition

concepts.name: Tax Expenditure: Exemptions, Deductions, and Revenue Foregone
key_dimensions: Definition of tax expenditure as implicit subsidy through the tax system
Revenue Foregone Statement in Union Budget: What it measures and its fiscal implications
UPSC trap: Tax expenditure does NOT appear as spending in budget but has same fiscal effect as direct subsidy
Key deductions: 80C, 80D, Section 10 exemptions — debate on whether these achieve intended policy goals

concepts.name: Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) to Dividend Taxation Shift
key_dimensions: Pre-2020: DDT paid by company at 15% — shareholder received tax-free dividend
Post-2020 abolition: Dividend now taxed in hands of shareholder at applicable income tax slab rate
UPSC trap: Classical system vs. dividend imputation system — India moved FROM integration BACK to classical
Impact on high-income shareholders, FIIs (treaty benefits), and corporate payout behavior

concepts.name: Taxation and Federalism: Divisible Pool, Cess, and Surcharge
key_dimensions: Article 270: Taxes levied and collected by Union, distributed between Union and States — divisible pool
UPSC trap: Cess and surcharge are NOT part of the divisible pool — states get NO share, hence fiscal grievance
Rising share of cess/surcharge in Union tax revenue — data trend and implications for fiscal federalism
Finance Commission's role in determining vertical and horizontal devolution from divisible pool

concepts.name: Tax-to-GDP Ratio: India's Performance and Structural Constraints
key_dimensions: India's tax-to-GDP (~11%) vs. OECD average (~34%) — structural reasons for the gap
Direct tax-to-GDP vs. indirect tax-to-GDP: What the ratio reveals about tax system quality
UPSC trap: High indirect tax share indicates regressive system; low direct tax share indicates narrow base
Measures to widen tax base: PAN-Aadhaar linking, faceless assessment, Annual Information Statement (AIS)

concepts.name: Laffer Curve and Optimal Taxation Theory
key_dimensions: Laffer Curve: Relationship between tax rates and tax revenue — concept of revenue-maximizing rate
Supply-side economics argument: Lower rates → higher compliance and economic activity → higher revenue
UPSC trap: Laffer Curve is theoretical; empirical evidence for India's optimal rate is contested
Application to corporate tax cut of 2019 and wealth tax abolition (2015) — were revenues actually higher?

concepts.name: Wealth Tax, Inheritance Tax, and Property Taxation in India
key_dimensions: Wealth Tax abolished in 2015 — replaced by surcharge on super-rich; rationale and criticism
Inheritance/estate duty: Abolished in 1985; recent political debates on reintroduction
UPSC trap: India has NO inheritance tax currently — contrast with US estate tax and UK inheritance tax
Property tax as a local body resource: Underutilization, 15th Finance Commission recommendations, and urban fiscal gap

concepts.name: Transfer Pricing and Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS)
key_dimensions: Transfer pricing: Manipulation of intra-group transactions to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions
OECD BEPS project: 15 Action Plans — India's adoption, particularly Action 13 (Country-by-Country Reporting)
UPSC trap: GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) vs. SAAR (Specific Anti-Avoidance Rule) — GAAR is broader and discretionary
Pillar Two (Global Minimum Tax of 15%): G20/OECD agreement and India's position/implementation status

concepts.name: Tax Avoidance vs. Tax Evasion: Legal Framework and GAAR
key_dimensions: Distinction: Evasion is illegal; avoidance is legal but may be impermissible under GAAR
GAAR (Chapter X-A of Income Tax Act): Conditions for invoking — impermissible avoidance arrangement
UPSC trap: GAAR can override tax treaty provisions (DTAA) in certain cases — significant for treaty shopping
Vodafone case, Cairn case: Retrospective taxation controversy and its resolution through Taxation Laws Amendment Act 2021

concepts.name: Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) and Tax Treaties
key_dimensions: Purpose of DTAA: Avoid double taxation, prevent tax evasion, promote investment — bilateral nature
Two methods: Exemption method vs. Tax credit method — India generally follows credit method
UPSC trap: DTAA overrides domestic tax law UNLESS domestic law is more beneficial to taxpayer (Section 90)
Mauritius/Singapore/Netherlands route: Historical treaty abuse, Limitation of Benefits (LOB) clauses introduced post-2016

concepts.name: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) and Taxation of Financial Markets
key_dimensions: STT: Levied on purchase/sale of equity shares, derivatives — collected at source by stock exchanges
Policy rationale: Curb speculation, ensure some tax even when capital gains are under-reported
UPSC trap: STT is a direct tax (though transaction-based) — payer cannot shift it easily unlike indirect taxes
Interaction with capital gains tax: STT payment is a condition for concessional STCG (15%) and LTCG (10%) rates on equity

concepts.name: Fiscal Drag and Inflation's Impact on Tax Revenues
key_dimensions: Fiscal drag (bracket creep): Inflation pushes taxpayers into higher slabs without real income gain
Buoyancy vs. elasticity of taxes: Tax buoyancy > 1 means tax grows faster than GDP — desirable
UPSC trap: GST has lower automatic stabilizer property than income tax — requires rate changes to adjust
India's tax buoyancy data: Direct taxes more buoyant than indirect taxes post-formalization; implications for fiscal policy
